headline: No Entry Permits Required; Check Seasonal Guided Walk Schedules
reservation: Access to the Torridon estate is open without a permit system for entry. However, the countryside centre is currently closed for review, and visitors interested in weekly guided walks during spring and summer should check for official updates on meeting points and availability.

days.title: Coastal Lowlands and Peaks

stops.name: Torridon
stops.detail: Begin at the countryside centre for low-level coastal walks or head to the loch-side hide for a chance to spot fishing otters.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours from the east; mountain road conditions vary significantly.
days.note: Pace your visit to allow for changing weather if attempting any of the five local Munros.

intel.title: Countryside Centre Status
intel.text: The countryside centre is currently undergoing a review and is closed for future planning. It remains a recommended starting point for low-level walks around the coast and estate.

intel.title: Guided Walk Availability
intel.text: Official guided walks are typically scheduled weekly during the spring and summer seasons. Check current Trust announcements for specific dates and departure times.

intel.title: Supply and Fuel Gaps
intel.text: Evidence does not specify fuel or charging availability within the estate boundaries. Verify refueling locations along the North Coast 500 route before entering the glen.

intel.title: Connectivity Status
intel.text: Cellular signal strength in the Torridon mountains is not documented in official sources. Download maps for offline use before arriving at the loch or trailheads.

intel.title: Parking Information
intel.text: The source does not provide specific parking capacities or fill times for the countryside centre or trailheads. Arrive early during peak summer months as spaces may be limited on the NC500 loop.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental in Inverness and stock up on supplies before heading west. Check-in logic depends on local guest houses as the countryside centre is closed.
plan.vehicle: Suitable for standard cars and smaller RVs via the NC500, but check for width restrictions on single-track mountain roads.
plan.goldenHour: Loch Torridon viewpoints offer significant sunset potential, though cloud cover is frequent in the Highlands.
